full_judgment:
2. The facts of the case giving rise to the Rule, in brief, are that the O.P. Md. Nurul Islam representing himself as Secretary, Fenchuganj Muktijudha Kollayan Samobaya Samitee filed an application under Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure in the Court of S.D.O. Sadar, Sylhet on 29-7-76 allegation inter alia that members of the said Samitee got separate settlements of the case land from the Government, and, having taken possession of the same, grew paddy which became ripe and petitioners was threatening to take away the paddy forcibly. So, the O. P. Nurul Islam prayed for restraining the petitioner and others by an order of injunction from interfering with possession of the O.P. Nurul Islam and his Co-sharers. 

 3. The Sub-divisional Magistrate at first initiated proceedings under Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure but on appearance of the petitioners the proceedings was converted into proceedings under Section 145 Cr.P.C. for the reason that the petitioners claimed right, interest and possession in the disputed land. By their application before the Sub-divisional Magistrate the petitioners made out the case that the disputed lands were accretions to their lands and they were entitled to get settlement of the same. They have been in possession of the land, and, on their prayer the proposed settlement in favour of the O.P. and others was stayed by the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Revenue, Sylhet.
